children: Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC)-based Raminvest Holding will undertake drilling at the Wompou Gold project in Mauritania.
Wompou covers 446 square kilometres (sq km) in the Mauritanide Belt and is held through the group's Mauritanian subsidiary under exploration permit 2265B2.
"Assay results of up to 50.14 g/t gold and six defined targets give us a sound basis to move Wompou into drilling," said Reda Rami, Chairman of Raminvest Holding.

The next stage is expected to include field verification, detailed geological and geochemical work and targeted drilling, subject to the required technical and regulatory approvals, before advancing toward resource definition and development studies.
The company is also advancing the Tabatanet project through its subsidiary Baraka Mines.
Covering 496 sq. km, the project gives the Group exposure to rare earth elements and niobium, minerals used in advanced manufacturing, high-performance materials, aerospace and electronics.

title: Dubai-based Raminvest Holding to start drilling at Mauritania gold project
